resubscribe_missing.title: Resubscribe missing items
resubscribe_missing.message:
This will process {count} Workshop items that are still subscribed but missing local files.

The manager will first send unsubscribe requests to Steam and wait for success, then subscribe again so Steam can fetch these items again.

Because Steam client and network state are outside the manager's control, unsubscribe may succeed while resubscribe fails, downloads may queue for a long time, or list refresh may be delayed. After running this, wait for Steam downloads to complete, then refresh inventory or scan again.

This will not unsubscribe them. It directly asks the Steam client to redownload or verify these items, then waits in the task bar until Steam confirms the local files are downloaded.

If Steam network is unavailable, downloads stay queued too long, or the item itself is unavailable, the task will fail.

backup_list.rules:
**[[Automatic and manual backups]]**
^^Short-term backups:^^ After each save or run action, the current config file is backed up when it changed. Short-term backups are kept for 1 day by default, cleaned on startup, and only the latest daily backup is kept as a long-term backup.
^^Long-term backups:^^ Automatic long-term backups are kept for the last 30 days by default. Expired files are removed.
^^Manual backups:^^ Manually created backups are saved to the selected directory and are not removed automatically.
__Automatic list backup format: RML_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.rml__
__Manual export support: ModsConfig.xml / ModList.rml__

group_list.help:
**Group management**
Drag mods from lists into any group.
Right-click a list to quickly move mods into or out of existing groups.
On the mod details page, you can manage all groups that contain that mod.

Groups work like a clipboard. Moving into or out of groups is a [[copy]] operation:
 - ^^Removing^^ from a group does not remove the mod itself;
 - Dragging mods between groups copies them and skips members already in the target group.

Whole groups can also be dragged:
 - Drag a group into the activated list to activate every mod in it;
 - Drag a group into the deactivated list to deactivate every mod in it.

mod_rule_editor.language_owner: Detected owners come from backend analysis by default. You can set owners manually. The right-side switch controls override or merge mode: when override is on, user owners replace detected owners; when off, they are merged with detected owners.

rule_panel.priority: Rule priority affects autosort and issue detection decisions.
rule_panel.weight:
**Mod weight rules**
Normal mods use weight 500 by default.
“Set weight” accepts 1-999. Smaller values sort earlier.
“Shift weight” accepts -999 to 999. Negative moves earlier, positive moves later, and the final value is clamped to 1-999.
“Top / Bottom” are effectively 0 and 1000 with higher priority. Use them only when a mod must be first or last.

Note: Top/bottom weights override other weight settings, including default and shifted weights.
      Weight shift is based on the normal mod weight by default. If another weight is set, shift is based on that value. Multiple shifts stack. Total weight is clamped to 1-999.

Suggested weight ranges:

[[Range]]		[[Category]]						[[Examples]]
0				Pinned top						Harmony or manual top
1 - 49			Very early frameworks			Frameworks near Harmony
50 - 99			Official content						Core, Royalty, Ideology, Anomaly
100 - 199		Common base libraries					Vanilla Expanded Framework
201 - 700		Normal gameplay/content mods		Most content mods (items, races, factions)
701 - 800		UI enhancements				RimHUD, Numbers, InventoryTab
801 - 899		Visual/audio/patches			Texture and audio replacements
900 - 949		Language/localization				LanguagePack
950 - 999		Late optimizers/logic		Rocketman, Performance Optimize
1000			Pinned bottom						Manual bottom

shortcut.message:
Create a desktop shortcut for profile "{name}"?
The shortcut will use this profile's current launch mode and be placed on the desktop.
If this profile prefers Steam launch and its game path differs from the default profile, the manager will update Steam non-Steam game shortcut configuration and create a Steam protocol shortcut on the desktop. Steam must be fully closed before writing, and restarted afterwards for this to take effect.
If multiple profiles share the same game directory, the shortcut can only guarantee the launch target and arguments are correct. It cannot guarantee that directory links always match this profile.
shortcut.title: Create desktop shortcut

steam_running_conflict.message:
This environment is set to launch the game executable directly, and Workshop mods have been linked into the local mod folder.
Steam is currently running. If you continue now, Steam will take over this launch and the game will show two copies of Workshop mods.
The local-folder copy is usually loaded first, so gameplay is usually unaffected, but the in-game list and later management can become confusing.
You can quit Steam manually. This window will keep waiting and launch the game automatically after Steam fully exits.
If you understand the impact, you can continue anyway.
steam_running_conflict.title: Quit Steam first
